correctness.rationale: From the original exact slow-Euler/fast-OU scheme the scalar recurrence is exact. Conditioning on independent position innovations gives an exact product moment identity. The compact positive self-adjoint Mehler-kernel operator has strictly positive top-eigenfunction overlap, so its top eigenvalue gives necessary and sufficient second-moment boundedness. Normalized Hermites prove strict increase in correlation because the inverse multiplier is not square-integrable at its zero sphere; strong OU-semigroup convergence gives the infinite-correlation endpoint. Exact Gaussian moments give the independent threshold and 25/24 rational witness. The standalone verifier passed 95 exact rational checks; finite tests do not prove the operator theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact, unique finite-correlation instability frontier for a concrete recently analyzed numerical sampling scheme, for every finite number of Gaussian probes. It exposes a structural and practically consequential distinction between preserving Gaussian probe marginals and preserving long-time second-moment stability. It also supplies an exact rational counterexample and a computable operator criterion for permissible OU correlation and step parameters; the claim does not overreach to general sampling ergodicity.
